muc.title: Type a sentence, get a clip
muc.text: Last time, AI watched video. Now flip it: AI makes video. Type a sentence: "a cat riding a cyclo through the old quarter". A moment later, there's a clip.

muc.title: Removing noise, remember?
muc.text: In the video about drawing pictures, AI started from a screen of grainy static and slowly cleaned it up to match your words. Video works the same way, but it cleans a whole stack of frames at once.

muc.title: The hard part: every frame must match
muc.text: The hard part is time. Clean each frame on its own, and the cat is black in one frame and orange in the next. So AI cleans the whole sequence at once, so each frame matches the next.

muc.title: Characters can't change faces
muc.text: That way, characters keep the same face and clothes, and the scene doesn't jump around. The longer the video, the harder this gets.

muc.title: Hands and text often break
muc.text: But hands are often drawn wrong: extra fingers, fingers stuck together. Text on signs gets warped, because AI draws the shape of letters instead of writing each one.

muc.title: Looks real, breaks the rules
muc.text: Physics often goes wrong too: a glass tips over but the water doesn't spill, a person walks through a door. AI copies what looks real, without truly understanding how the world works.

muc.title: A 4-part video prompt
muc.text: Write a prompt with four parts: subject, action, camera angle, lighting. For example: an old woman selling sticky rice, wrapping it in banana leaves, close-up shot, early morning sun. Make a 5-second clip first, and only make it longer once you like it.

muc.title: All in one brain?
muc.text: Listening, talking, watching, making video. It's all coming together into one brain. How well can a brain like that understand you? See you in part 6, the last part.
